resources.string: Scan labels. Check consistency. Trace origin.
Photograph or choose a picture of a label, carton or barcode.
Runs on your phone. Your photo is not uploaded. Without an AI vision model, text recognition is weaker. Use Gemini AI mode for the most accurate data.
Gemini has vision models that read data, analyze images and translate better than offline mode.
Add a Gemini API key to use Gemini mode.
• Fill the frame with the label.\n• Avoid glare and shadows.\n• Photograph barcodes and QR codes close-up, separately.
Looking for barcodes and QR codes…
Reading label text on your phone…
Asking Gemini to read the label…
The label is internally consistent and matches everything we could check.
Serious inconsistencies were found. Verify with the manufacturer before relying on this product.
Too little readable information. Try a clearer, closer photo.
For reference only. A photo cannot prove a product is genuine. Confirm with the manufacturer or an authorized seller.
Based only on the label and public databases. Shipping and distribution steps cannot be seen from a photo.
Standards printed on a label are the manufacturer’s own claims. The app does not verify certificates.
The voice for this language is not installed. Install it in your phone’s text-to-speech settings.
No favorites yet. Tap the heart on a result.
Paste keys here, one per line
Keys are encrypted on this device and shown masked. They are tried in order; if one reaches its limit, the next is used.
How to get a free API key
Open aistudio.google.com/apikey and sign in with your Google account.
If asked, choose or create a Google Cloud project. The default one is fine.
Come back here, paste it in the box above (one key per line) and tap Save keys.
Never share your key. If it leaks, delete it in AI Studio and create a new one.
The free quota is limited and may change. Google’s terms apply.
In Gemini mode, the photo you choose is sent to Google’s Gemini API using your own key and is handled under Google’s terms. Nothing is sent in Offline mode.
Open Scan and tap Take photo or Choose image. Fill the frame with the label, carton or barcode.
Offline reads text on your phone. Gemini reads handwriting and mixed-language labels better, but needs your own API key and internet.
The score shows how consistent the label is. Green is good, amber needs checking, red is serious.
If a barcode or QR is visible, the app checks its digits and country prefix, then compares the product in public databases with the packaging.
Overview, Specifications, Authenticity, Supply chain and Legal & certificates show the details.
Tap Listen to hear the summary. The speed is 2× by default and can go up to 4×.
Every scan is saved on your phone only. Tap the heart to keep important products in Favorites.
A photo cannot prove a product is genuine. Treat the result as a hint and confirm with the manufacturer or an authorized seller.

Code %1$s: the check digit is valid.

GS1 prefix %1$s is registered in %2$s. This does not prove where it was made.
The label says origin %1$s, but the barcode prefix belongs to %2$s. This can be normal; please verify.
Check code %1$s on Verified by GS1 to see which company it is licensed to. If GS1 has no record, that does not by itself mean the product is fake.
Not found in %1$s. This does not mean fake, only that it is not recorded.

The packaging text differs from the database product name “%1$s”.
The database says %1$s, but that quantity was not seen on the packaging.
The QR contains a link to %1$s. The app never opens it automatically; check it is the maker’s official domain.
The link uses a URL shortener that hides the real site.
The link points to a raw IP address.
The domain has look-alike characters (xn--) and could be an imitation.
The QR is a GS1 Digital Link for code %1$s.
This code was read by AI from the printed digits, not scanned directly. Treat it with lower confidence.
IMEI %1$s passes the Luhn check. This only checks the number format; it does not prove the IMEI is real or registered.
IMEI %1$s fails the Luhn check: a digit may be misread or the number may be wrong. Retake a sharper photo and compare it with the number on the device (dial *#06#).
